### Motivation and Context

Fixes #3947.

Supersedes #8281 with a clean DCO-signed history. This continues #7761, with the original implementation by @ogulcanaydogan and follow-up work from #8281.

MVN opset 29 adds configurable `epsilon` (default `1e-9`) and changes the numerical contract: it computes centered population variance, promotes FLOAT16/BFLOAT16 intermediates to FLOAT, then casts the output back to the input type. Versioned reference implementations also support unannotated nodes and model-local functions, including linked epsilon attributes.

The 28→29 converter expands legacy MVN into primitives rather than selecting the new schema, preserving its `E[X²] - E[X]²` computation and input-type arithmetic. The reverse expansion preserves v29's centered variance, epsilon, and promotion. Opsets 9 and 13 retain their existing computation; the v13 documentation is intentionally clarified to show its already-used `1e-9` epsilon, not left textually unchanged.

Captured-tensor metadata propagation runs before version conversions generally, filling missing type/shape annotations in nested graphs without overwriting existing capture annotations. MVN's type-dependent adapters need this metadata for outer-scope inputs and initializer-only captures. The pass stores local metadata in parent-linked lexical scopes and resolves captured names from the nearest enclosing binding, without copying ancestor maps for each branch.

Direct function retrieval, validation, and execution cover the registered function opsets 13 and 18 and the default opset-29 path, which selects the 18 builder. Linked empty axes exposed a reference ReduceMean-13 normalization bug; the fix makes it match literal empty axes and reduce all dimensions.

issue.title: [Feature request] Support multi-axis blocked DequantizeLinear for 2-D FP8 weight tiles
issue.body:
## Request

Please consider a first-class multi-axis blocked dequantization contract for already-typed FP8 tensors with compact 2-D scale grids, e.g. 128×128 weight tiles. This could extend `DequantizeLinear` (and symmetrically `QuantizeLinear`) with a block-shape vector, or use another agreed standard representation.

This is **not** a claim that the arithmetic is impossible in ONNX. It is a request for a direct, validated quantization boundary that exporters and runtimes can recognize without expanding scales or reverse-engineering a reshape/broadcast/cast/multiply graph.

## Concrete model use case

While adding and validating [fishaudio/drama-3](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3) in [onnxruntime/mobius#793](https://github.com/onnxruntime/mobius/pull/793), we encountered expert weights stored as:

- `FLOAT8E4M3FN` matrices `[O, I]`;
- separate FP32 scales `[ceil(O/128), ceil(I/128)]`;
- no affine integer codes or zero points;
- checkpoint metadata: `quant_method="bsgemm-moe"`, `weight_block_size=[128,128]`.

For example, real expert gate/up weights have shape `[512,2048]` with scales `[4,16]`; down weights have shape `[2048,512]` with scales `[16,4]`. The text backbone has 40 MoE layers, 256 experts per layer and top-8 routing.

The intended weight-value semantics are:

```text
W[o,i] = float32(Wq[o,i]) * S[floor(o/128), floor(i/128)]
```

A stacked expert bank generalizes this to `Wq[E,O,I]` and `S[E,ceil(O/128),ceil(I/128)]`, with no blocking across the expert axis.

Checkpoint revision: `b2b5ee998034b2975720906c815e7fb0e9f007bd`.

Our explicitly dequantized FP32 fallback is correct: the complete checkpoint passed H200 CUDA prefill/cached-logit comparison and 20 exact greedy token-frame matches against independent upstream inference. It serialized about 143.8 GB. That figure describes **our chosen fallback**, not an unavoidable ONNX memory/storage requirement or a benchmark of the new grouped operator.

## Current DequantizeLinear limitation

[DequantizeLinear-28](https://onnx.ai/onnx/operators/onnx__DequantizeLinear.html) provides one `axis` and one `block_size`. Its blocked scale shape must equal the input shape except along that one axis.

A minimal example is:

```text
Wq: FLOAT8E4M3FN[256,256]
S:  FLOAT[2,2]
S = [[1,2], [3,4]]
Wq = all ones
```

The desired output is four 128×128 quadrants containing 1, 2, 3 and 4.

Neither of these directly describes that grid:

```text
DequantizeLinear(Wq, S, axis=0, block_size=128)
DequantizeLinear(Wq, S, axis=1, block_size=128)
```

Using the ONNX reference evaluator with the opset-28 schema, both are rejected with:

```text
Invalid shapes for Blocked Quantization. Input 2 shape should identical to
Input 1 shape, except for one dimension, in which blocking is performed
```

`axis=0` instead needs scales `[2,256]`; `axis=1` needs `[256,2]`.

## Existing workarounds and why a standard boundary helps

There are valid current-standard decompositions:

1. Repeat the compact `[2,2]` scales into `[256,2]`, then use ordinary blocked DQ along axis 1. We verified this produces the intended quadrants, but uses 512 scale entries instead of 4 (or requires a scale-expansion subgraph).
2. Reshape the FP8 tensor to `[O_blocks,128,I_blocks,128]`, reshape scales to `[O_blocks,1,I_blocks,1]`, then cast/multiply/broadcast and reshape back. This preserves the mathematical result and can retain the original FP8 initializer, but does not expose a direct multi-axis Q/DQ contract.

A good runtime may optimize these graphs already. The request is to make the block geometry and precision semantics explicit and portable to quantization tooling and fusion passes, rather than mandate full materialization or promise that an op alone guarantees a fast kernel.

## Suggested requirements

- Describe multiple blocked axes, e.g. an optional `block_shape=[128,128]` for a matrix or `[1,128,128]` for an expert bank, with explicit scale-grid validation.
- Define partial edge tiles using ceil-divided scale extents, while preserving existing scalar/per-axis/single-axis-blocked behavior.
- Preserve FP8 numeric storage and FP32 scale semantics. Specify multiplication/output precision; FP32 multiplication followed by an explicit cast must remain expressible without changing decoded weight values.
- Make the composition with `MatMul` / `GroupedMatMul` recognizable, so runtimes may fuse dequantization with selected-expert computation without first creating a dense float bank.
- Include reference/shape tests for both blocked axes, invalid grids, omitted zero points and output casts. Alternatively, document a canonical existing-op mapping if that is preferred to a schema extension.

## Relationship to existing work

- [GroupedMatMul-29](https://onnx.ai/onnx/operators/onnx__GroupedMatMul.html) and merged [onnx/onnx#8556](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/pull/8556) already address the float grouped-execution boundary. I am **not** requesting that operator again. Its documentation recommends composing weight-only quantization through DQ; compact multi-axis FP8 scales are the specific gap here.
- [onnx/onnx#7902](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/issues/7902) / [onnx/onnx#8370](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/issues/8370) provide the broader MoE/interchange context.
- [onnx/onnx#8359](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/issues/8359) concerns encoded external/block-quantized storage. This request is narrower: the payload is already a standard FP8 tensor plus a standard FP32 tensor, so no opaque GGUF codec or new tensor encoding is required.
- `LinearAttention` and `CausalConvWithState` already exist in opset 27; runtime/exporter adoption of those is separate and is not reported here as a missing ONNX feature.

issue.body:
### Motivation and Context

Recent models such as [Qwen3.5-35B-A3B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B) are available in [community GGUF distributions](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GGUF) with packed quantized weights. `DequantizePacked` lets importers retain these payloads as UINT8 initializers, including external data, rather than expanding weights during export.

```text
y = DequantizePacked<format, shape, output_dtype=FLOAT>(x)
```

- `x` is a rank-one UINT8 tensor containing one packed tensor payload with little-endian fields.
- `format` selects one of 27 fixed GGUF profiles across conventional GGML, K-quant, IQ, ternary, MXFP4, and NVFP4 encodings. Identifiers such as `gguf:q4_0` accept no parameters.
- `shape` specifies static dimensions in ONNX order, with a block-aligned last dimension.
- `output_dtype` supports FLOAT (default), FLOAT16, BFLOAT16, and DOUBLE. Decoding uses FLOAT arithmetic followed by one output conversion.

The [in-tree specification](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/19b091202765d5d444acd9d9c25a0b81eef474b5/docs/DequantizePacked.md) defines byte layouts, decoding arithmetic, and complete IQ codebooks. GGUF profiles follow [GGML revision da8e2a54](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/tree/da8e2a54b919557b816b1c2beb432ccb766f7ce0), quantization version 2. File parsing and model-specific permutations remain importer steps.

Includes schema/type/shape inference, NumPy reference decoding, tests, and generated documentation. GGML-derived tables and algorithms retain their MIT notices. The speculative `onnx:nf4` family has been removed; NF4 and bitsandbytes nested scales can instead use codebook lookup and arithmetic with existing ONNX operators.

issue.title: `optimize_for_ort` fuses group norms into `com.microsoft.GroupNorm`, which has no CPU kernel and only some CUDA shapes
issue.body:
`optimize_for_ort` fuses every group norm into ONNX Runtime's `com.microsoft.GroupNorm` (the `instance_to_group_normalization` rules in `ORT_PATTERN_REWRITE_RULES`), but that op has no CPU kernel, and its CUDA kernel only takes some channel / group counts. An exported `torch.nn.GroupNorm` that runs on both providers before the fusion fails on the CPU for every shape afterwards, and on CUDA for 32 channels in 32 groups or 40 channels in 8. We hit it on Chameleon, Emu3 (VQ-VAE) and the DETR backbones (Conditional / Deformable DETR). Gating the rule on the target provider and on the shapes the CUDA kernel accepts (or leaving it out of the default rules) would fix it.

**Repro** (onnxscript 0.7.2, onnxruntime-gpu 1.29.0, torch 2.13, A100):

```python
"""onnxscript's `optimize_for_ort` fuses every group norm into ONNX Runtime's `com.microsoft.GroupNorm`, which has no
CPU kernel and whose CUDA kernel only takes some channel / group counts: an exported `torch.nn.GroupNorm` that runs
before the fusion no longer runs after it, on the CPU at all, and on CUDA for 32 channels in 32 groups or 40 in 8."""

import numpy as np
import onnx_ir as ir
import onnxruntime as ort
import onnxscript
import torch
from onnxscript.rewriter.ort_fusions import optimize_for_ort


def run(model, provider, x) -> str:
    try:
        session = ort.InferenceSession(ir.to_proto(model).SerializeToString(), providers=[provider])
        session.run(None, {session.get_inputs()[0].name: x})
        return "runs"
    except Exception as error:
        message = str(error).splitlines()[0]
        return "fails: " + message.split("Status Message: ")[-1].split(" : ")[-1]


print("onnxscript", onnxscript.__version__, "| onnxruntime", ort.__version__, "| torch", torch.__version__)
for groups, channels in ((32, 320), (32, 32), (8, 40)):
    x = torch.randn(2, channels, 4, 4)
    model = torch.onnx.export(torch.nn.GroupNorm(groups, channels).eval(), (x,), dynamo=True).model
    print(f"GroupNorm({groups}, {channels})")
    for provider in ("CPUExecutionProvider", "CUDAExecutionProvider"):

    optimize_for_ort(model)
    print("  fused ops:", sorted({node.op_type for node in model.graph}))
    for provider in ("CPUExecutionProvider", "CUDAExecutionProvider"):
        print(f"  {provider:22s} fused:    {run(model, provider, x.numpy())}")
```

issue.title: ShapeInferencePass turns an untyped sequence value into a tensor
issue.body:
`ShapeInferencePass` merges the inferred types back with `value.dtype = inferred_value.dtype` (`_merge_func` in `passes/common/shape_inference.py`). On a value with no type yet, the `dtype` setter creates a `TensorType`, so a value onnx infers as a sequence comes back as a tensor. A `SequenceEmpty` output then reads `tensor(float)`, and ONNX Runtime rejects the model. `onnx.shape_inference.infer_shapes` alone keeps it valid.

We hit it on a `Loop` carrying a tensor sequence (how torchlib exports `embedding_bag`): ONNX Runtime fails with `Loop ... Type mismatch. Current=1 Input=4` (a tensor where the loop takes a sequence). Copying `inferred_value.type` when the original value has no type would fix it.

**Repro** (onnx-ir 1.1.0, onnx 1.23.2, onnxruntime 1.31.1):

```python
"""onnx_ir's `ShapeInferencePass` types a `Loop` body's sequence output as a tensor: a loop carrying a tensor sequence
(`SequenceEmpty`, then `SequenceInsert` in the body) no longer loads in ONNX Runtime after the pass, while
`onnx.shape_inference.infer_shapes` keeps it valid."""

import numpy as np
import onnx
import onnx_ir as ir
import onnxruntime as ort
from onnx import TensorProto, helper
from onnx_ir.passes.common import ShapeInferencePass

sequence = helper.make_tensor_sequence_value_info
body = helper.make_graph(
    [
        helper.make_node("Identity", ["cond_in"], ["cond_out"]),
        helper.make_node("SequenceInsert", ["sequence_in", "x"], ["sequence_out"]),
    ],
    "body",
    [
        helper.make_tensor_value_info("iteration", TensorProto.INT64, []),
        helper.make_tensor_value_info("cond_in", TensorProto.BOOL, []),
        sequence("sequence_in", TensorProto.FLOAT, None),
    ],
    [helper.make_tensor_value_info("cond_out", TensorProto.BOOL, []), sequence("sequence_out", TensorProto.FLOAT, None)],
)
graph = helper.make_graph(
    [
        helper.make_node("SequenceEmpty", [], ["empty"], dtype=TensorProto.FLOAT),
        helper.make_node("Loop", ["trip_count", "cond", "empty"], ["sequence"], body=body),
        helper.make_node("ConcatFromSequence", ["sequence"], ["y"], axis=0),
    ],
    "g",
    [
        helper.make_tensor_value_info("x", TensorProto.FLOAT, [2]),
        helper.make_tensor_value_info("trip_count", TensorProto.INT64, []),
        helper.make_tensor_value_info("cond", TensorProto.BOOL, []),
    ],
    [helper.make_tensor_value_info("y", TensorProto.FLOAT, None)],
)
proto = helper.make_model(graph, opset_imports=[helper.make_opsetid("", 18)], ir_version=10)
feeds = {"x": np.ones(2, np.float32), "trip_count": np.array(3, np.int64), "cond": np.array(True)}


def run(model: onnx.ModelProto) -> str:
    try:
        session = ort.InferenceSession(model.SerializeToString(), providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"])
        return f"runs, y = {session.run(None, feeds)[0]}"
    except Exception as error:
        return f"fails: {str(error).splitlines()[0][:160]}"


print("onnx", onnx.__version__, "| onnx_ir", ir.__version__, "| onnxruntime", ort.__version__)
print("original:                     ", run(proto))
print("onnx.shape_inference:         ", run(onnx.shape_inference.infer_shapes(proto)))
model = ir.from_proto(proto)
ShapeInferencePass()(model)
print("onnx_ir ShapeInferencePass:   ", run(ir.to_proto(model)))
loop_body = next(node for node in model.graph if node.op_type == "Loop").attributes["body"].value
print("body output type after pass:  ", loop_body.outputs[1].type)
```

Output:

```
onnx 1.23.2 | onnx_ir 1.1.0 | onnxruntime 1.31.1
original:                      runs, y = [1. 1. 1. 1. 1. 1.]
onnx.shape_inference:          runs, y = [1. 1. 1. 1. 1. 1.]
onnx_ir ShapeInferencePass:    fails: [ONNXRuntimeError] : 1 : FAIL : Type Error: Type (tensor(float)) of output arg (empty) of node () does not match expected type (seq(tensor(float))).
body output type after pass:   Sequence(Tensor(FLOAT))
```

issue.title: feat(defs): add epsilon to MeanVarianceNormalization in opset 29
issue.body:
### Motivation and Context

Fixes #3947.

Supersedes #8281 with a clean DCO-signed history. This continues #7761, with the original implementation by @ogulcanaydogan and follow-up work from #8281.

MVN opset 29 adds configurable `epsilon` (default `1e-9`) and changes the numerical contract: it computes centered population variance, promotes FLOAT16/BFLOAT16 intermediates to FLOAT, then casts the output back to the input type. Versioned reference implementations also support unannotated nodes and model-local functions, including linked epsilon attributes.

The 28→29 converter expands legacy MVN into primitives rather than selecting the new schema, preserving its `E[X²] - E[X]²` computation and input-type arithmetic. The reverse expansion preserves v29's centered variance, epsilon, and promotion. Opsets 9 and 13 retain their existing computation; the v13 documentation is intentionally clarified to show its already-used `1e-9` epsilon, not left textually unchanged.

Captured-tensor metadata propagation runs before version conversions generally, filling missing type/shape annotations in nested graphs without overwriting existing capture annotations. MVN's type-dependent adapters need this metadata for outer-scope inputs and initializer-only captures. The pass stores local metadata in parent-linked lexical scopes and resolves captured names from the nearest enclosing binding, without copying ancestor maps for each branch.

Direct function retrieval, validation, and execution cover the registered function opsets 13 and 18 and the default opset-29 path, which selects the 18 builder. Linked empty axes exposed a reference ReduceMean-13 normalization bug; the fix makes it match literal empty axes and reduce all dimensions.

issue.body:
### Motivation and Context

Qwen Gated DeltaNet layers can have more value/state heads than query/key heads. LinearAttention-27 couples the key and value head counts, so exporting their native projections requires explicit adjacent Q/K expansion before the recurrent operation.

Add LinearAttention-29 with optional `v_num_heads`. Its default of zero preserves the existing query-GQA/MQA contract. A positive value requires `q_num_heads == kv_num_heads` and a value-head count divisible by the compact key-head count. Value/state head `h` reads compact Q/K head `floor(h / (v_num_heads / kv_num_heads))`, matching adjacent `repeat_interleave`, not whole-axis tiling. Output, recurrent state, decay and beta use the value-head count.

The following configurations map directly to `update_rule="gated_delta"` with `q_num_heads=kv_num_heads=16`:

| Model | `v_num_heads` | Adjacent expansion factor |
|---|---:|---:|
| [Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct/blob/9c7f2fbe84465e40164a94cc16cd30b6999b0cc7/config.json) | 32 | 2 |
| [Qwen3.8-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0/config.json) | 48 | 3 |
| [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next/blob/de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540/config.json) | 48 | 3 |
| [Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B/blob/207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996/config.json) | 128 | 8 |

The [pinned Qwen3-Next implementation](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c27795950091cdaf1b0e32c4aed58618fb41ffa0/src/transformers/models/qwen3_next/modeling_qwen3_next.py#L648-L764) expands compact Q/K into value-head groups. Its [sequential recurrence](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c27795950091cdaf1b0e32c4aed58618fb41ffa0/src/transformers/models/qwen3_next/modeling_qwen3_next.py#L507-L566) decays the state, computes the delta against that decayed state, writes the update, then reads the output. Flash-Next's [`qwen4_exp` implementation](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c27795950091cdaf1b0e32c4aed58618fb41ffa0/src/transformers/models/qwen4_exp/modular_qwen4_exp.py#L322-L327) inherits Qwen3.5 Gated DeltaNet and changes the surrounding gated normalization.

For the 16-to-48 and 16-to-128 layouts with 128-dimensional heads, Q/K remain packed `[B,T,2048]`, values and output are `[B,T,6144]` or `[B,T,16384]`, and the carried state is `[B,48,128,128]` or `[B,128,128,128]`. Supplying FP32 `past_state` preserves FP32 recurrent state with FP16/BF16 activations. Causal convolution, Q/K normalization, gate projections, output gating and projections remain surrounding graph operations; the operator's query scale is applied once.

Explicit adjacent expansion followed by LinearAttention-27 is numerically sufficient and can also be fused by runtimes. This extension makes the native compact inputs and their exact head mapping part of the recurrent contract, so an exporter can retain the original projection widths and a runtime can consume that layout directly.

Relates to #8757: Mamba speculative verification also needs the recurrent state after each candidate token, rather than only the final state. Add optional third output `states` with shape `[B,T,H_state,Dk,Dv]`, available with every update rule and head mapping. Snapshot `t` follows that token's complete decay/update; the last snapshot equals `present_state`. The state dtype is preserved, including FP32 state with FP16/BF16 activations, without rounding the internal FP32 recurrence between snapshots. An empty chunk returns an empty trajectory and retains the initial or zero state.

The caller supplies the initial state and uses `Gather` on the time axis to select an accepted nonempty prefix; if none is accepted, it retains the initial state. The interface remains purely functional: no mutation, hidden persistent state, acceptance policy, commit/rollback API, convolution extension, or fused Mamba block. Omitting `states` preserves the existing two-output behavior without trajectory collection; requesting it adds storage proportional to the trajectory size.

The change preserves the opset-27 schema, adds shared named inference and function-body helpers, implements both extensions in the reference evaluator and standard-op decomposition, and permits downgrade when the value-head attribute is redundant and the trajectory is omitted.

Opsets 27/28 retain their historical zero-width key/value support. Opset 29 requires positive head widths, so upgrading known zero-width inputs is rejected; downgrading requires compatible head counts and an omitted trajectory. Compact input Q/K heads and value/state heads are separate in the schema and decomposition.

The shared function-expansion and inliner fixes also affect other function-based operators: nested captures and passthrough subgraph outputs retain lexical bindings, and omitted input/output slots retain their positional meaning. These fixes are covered independently of LinearAttention.

### Checklist

- [ ] The human author has reviewed this PR in full and takes responsibility for its content.

issue.title: feat(math): add numerically stable Expm1 in opset 29
issue.body:
### Motivation and Context

Propose `Expm1` in opset 29 as the companion to `Log1p` in #8710. It computes `exp(x) - 1` while preserving small nonzero results near zero.

For example, FLOAT `x = 1e-8` gives zero with `Sub(Exp(x), 1)`: the intermediate exponential rounds to exactly one. `Expm1(x)` retains a result near `1e-8`. The same cancellation occurs at larger input magnitudes in FLOAT16 and BFLOAT16, making a stable primitive useful for training and mixed-precision graphs.

Concrete uses include:

- The negative branches of ELU and SELU, which contain `alpha * (exp(x) - 1)`. ONNX's reference implementations already use `np.expm1` after #8355; the primitive lets exported graphs express that stable computation directly.
- Small exponential increments in scientific computing, including relaxation updates, exponential integrators, and rate/probability expressions such as `-expm1(-t)`.
- Exporting source-framework `expm1` operations without replacing them with a cancellation-prone `Exp -> Sub` graph.

### Operator definition

`y = Expm1(x)` accepts FLOAT16, BFLOAT16, FLOAT, and DOUBLE tensors and preserves shape and element type, including scalar and empty tensors. The self-contained schema specifies the real-valued expression, signed zeros, infinities, NaNs, overflow, and preservation of representable small results. Its numerical contract follows the approach in #8710, allowing backend algorithms and floating-point approximation without requiring bitwise agreement or correctly rounded transcendental results.

The proposal adds a NumPy reference implementation and backend cases with independent Python `math.expm1` expected values. Small-result cases use zero absolute tolerance so that an incorrect zero cannot pass. Dedicated tests also check signed zeros, dtype/shape preservation, overflow, full model checking, shape inference, and version conversion. There is no downgrade to opset 28.

### Why there is no fallback function body

`Exp -> Sub` loses the accuracy this operator provides. A native primitive preserves that numerical intent and maps to the existing `expm1` facilities in numerical libraries.

### Validation

- C++ Release build succeeded.
- 2,077 regression tests passed (65 skipped, 2 xpassed), covering reference evaluation, shape inference, automatic version conversion, and Sphinx operator integration.
- All 14 Expm1 backend reference cases passed (14 device variants skipped).
- Ruff, clang-format, and `git diff --check` passed; operator documentation and test coverage were regenerated.

### Checklist

- [x] The human author has reviewed this PR in full and takes responsibility for its content.

The reference result now takes zero-valued elements directly from the input, preserving both zero signs independently of NumPy behavior. Direct GPU tensor bindings remain experimental and opt-in. Use separate processes when combining them with another Apple-GPU execution provider.


issue.body:
### Motivation and Context

Qwen Gated DeltaNet layers can have more value/state heads than query/key heads. LinearAttention-27 couples the key and value head counts, so exporting their native projections requires explicit adjacent Q/K expansion before the recurrent operation.

Add LinearAttention-29 with optional `v_num_heads`. Its default of zero preserves the existing query-GQA/MQA contract. A positive value requires `q_num_heads == kv_num_heads` and a value-head count divisible by the compact key-head count. Value/state head `h` reads compact Q/K head `floor(h / (v_num_heads / kv_num_heads))`, matching adjacent `repeat_interleave`, not whole-axis tiling. Output, recurrent state, decay and beta use the value-head count.

The following configurations map directly to `update_rule="gated_delta"` with `q_num_heads=kv_num_heads=16`:

| Model | `v_num_heads` | Adjacent expansion factor |
|---|---:|---:|
| [Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct/blob/9c7f2fbe84465e40164a94cc16cd30b6999b0cc7/config.json) | 32 | 2 |
| [Qwen3.8-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0/config.json) | 48 | 3 |
| [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next/blob/de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540/config.json) | 48 | 3 |
| [Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B/blob/207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996/config.json) | 128 | 8 |

The [pinned Qwen3-Next implementation](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c27795950091cdaf1b0e32c4aed58618fb41ffa0/src/transformers/models/qwen3_next/modeling_qwen3_next.py#L648-L764) expands compact Q/K into value-head groups. Its [sequential recurrence](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c27795950091cdaf1b0e32c4aed58618fb41ffa0/src/transformers/models/qwen3_next/modeling_qwen3_next.py#L507-L566) decays the state, computes the delta against that decayed state, writes the update, then reads the output. Flash-Next's [`qwen4_exp` implementation](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c27795950091cdaf1b0e32c4aed58618fb41ffa0/src/transformers/models/qwen4_exp/modular_qwen4_exp.py#L322-L327) inherits Qwen3.5 Gated DeltaNet and changes the surrounding gated normalization.

For the 16-to-48 and 16-to-128 layouts with 128-dimensional heads, Q/K remain packed `[B,T,2048]`, values and output are `[B,T,6144]` or `[B,T,16384]`, and the carried state is `[B,48,128,128]` or `[B,128,128,128]`. Supplying FP32 `past_state` preserves FP32 recurrent state with FP16/BF16 activations. Causal convolution, Q/K normalization, gate projections, output gating and projections remain surrounding graph operations; the operator's query scale is applied once.

Explicit adjacent expansion followed by LinearAttention-27 is numerically sufficient and can also be fused by runtimes. This extension makes the native compact inputs and their exact head mapping part of the recurrent contract, so an exporter can retain the original projection widths and a runtime can consume that layout directly.

Relates to #8757: Mamba speculative verification also needs the recurrent state after each candidate token, rather than only the final state. Add optional third output `states` with shape `[B,T,H_state,Dk,Dv]`, available with every update rule and head mapping. Snapshot `t` follows that token's complete decay/update; the last snapshot equals `present_state`. The state dtype is preserved, including FP32 state with FP16/BF16 activations, without rounding the internal FP32 recurrence between snapshots. An empty chunk returns an empty trajectory and retains the initial or zero state.

The caller supplies the initial state and uses `Gather` on the time axis to select an accepted nonempty prefix; if none is accepted, it retains the initial state. The interface remains purely functional: no mutation, hidden persistent state, acceptance policy, commit/rollback API, convolution extension, or fused Mamba block. Omitting `states` preserves the existing two-output behavior without trajectory collection; requesting it adds storage proportional to the trajectory size.

The change preserves the opset-27 schema, adds shared named inference and function-body helpers, implements both extensions in the reference evaluator and standard-op decomposition, and permits downgrade when the value-head attribute is redundant and the trajectory is omitted.

Opsets 27/28 retain their historical zero-width key/value support. Opset 29 requires positive head widths, so upgrading known zero-width inputs is rejected; downgrading requires compatible head counts and an omitted trajectory. Compact input Q/K heads and value/state heads are separate in the schema and decomposition.

The shared function-expansion and inliner fixes also affect other function-based operators: nested captures and passthrough subgraph outputs retain lexical bindings, and omitted input/output slots retain their positional meaning. These fixes are covered independently of LinearAttention.

### Checklist

- [ ] The human author has reviewed this PR in full and takes responsibility for its content.

### Motivation and Context

Fixes #3947.

Supersedes #8281 with a clean DCO-signed history. This continues #7761, with the original implementation by @ogulcanaydogan and follow-up work from #8281.

MVN opset 29 adds configurable `epsilon` (default `1e-9`) and changes the numerical contract: it computes centered population variance, promotes FLOAT16/BFLOAT16 intermediates to FLOAT, then casts the output back to the input type. Versioned reference implementations also support unannotated nodes and model-local functions, including linked epsilon attributes.

The 28→29 converter expands legacy MVN into primitives rather than selecting the new schema, preserving its `E[X²] - E[X]²` computation and input-type arithmetic. The reverse expansion preserves v29's centered variance, epsilon, and promotion. Opsets 9 and 13 retain their existing computation; the v13 documentation is intentionally clarified to show its already-used `1e-9` epsilon, not left textually unchanged.

Captured-tensor metadata propagation runs before version conversions generally, filling missing type/shape annotations in nested graphs without overwriting existing capture annotations. MVN's type-dependent adapters need this metadata for outer-scope inputs and initializer-only captures. The pass stores local metadata in parent-linked lexical scopes and resolves captured names from the nearest enclosing binding, without copying ancestor maps for each branch.

Direct function retrieval, validation, and execution cover the registered function opsets 13 and 18 and the default opset-29 path, which selects the 18 builder. Linked empty axes exposed a reference ReduceMean-13 normalization bug; the fix makes it match literal empty axes and reduce all dimensions.

issue.title: feat(defs): add epsilon to MeanVarianceNormalization in opset 29
issue.body:
### Motivation and Context

Fixes #3947.

Supersedes #8281 with a clean DCO-signed history. This continues #7761, with the original implementation by @ogulcanaydogan and follow-up work from #8281.

MVN opset 29 adds configurable `epsilon` (default `1e-9`) and changes the numerical contract: it computes centered population variance, promotes FLOAT16/BFLOAT16 intermediates to FLOAT, then casts the output back to the input type. Versioned reference implementations also support unannotated nodes and model-local functions, including linked epsilon attributes.

The 28→29 converter expands legacy MVN into primitives rather than selecting the new schema, preserving its `E[X²] - E[X]²` computation and input-type arithmetic. The reverse expansion preserves v29's centered variance, epsilon, and promotion. Opsets 9 and 13 retain their existing computation; the v13 documentation is intentionally clarified to show its already-used `1e-9` epsilon, not left textually unchanged.

Captured-tensor metadata propagation runs before version conversions generally, filling missing type/shape annotations in nested graphs without overwriting existing capture annotations. MVN's type-dependent adapters need this metadata for outer-scope inputs and initializer-only captures. The pass stores local metadata in parent-linked lexical scopes and resolves captured names from the nearest enclosing binding, without copying ancestor maps for each branch.

Direct function retrieval, validation, and execution cover the registered function opsets 13 and 18 and the default opset-29 path, which selects the 18 builder. Linked empty axes exposed a reference ReduceMean-13 normalization bug; the fix makes it match literal empty axes and reduce all dimensions.

### Checklist

- [x] The human author has reviewed this PR in full and takes responsibility for its content.

comment.body: Addressed the current review summary with a documentation-only correction: v13 now states variance = ReduceMean(X^2, axes) - mean^2, matching both legacy function bodies and the legacy reference implementation. The prior centered expression is algebraically equivalent over real numbers but can differ under floating-point cancellation; it no longer appears as the v13 computation. V29 continues to specify centered variance. No function body, adapter, or numerical behavior changed.

### Motivation and Context

Relates to #5100.

Add `reduction="mean"` to `ScatterElements` and `ScatterND` in opset 29 to represent scatter mean reductions. Each destination averages its original data value with all updates targeting it. Integer results round toward negative infinity, and untouched elements retain their original values.

Keep this proposal focused on mean reduction without adding an `include_self` attribute. Existing reductions and historical schemas remain unchanged. Update the reference implementations, shape inference, version conversion, tests, and generated documentation; reject downgrading mean reduction to opset 28.

### Checklist

- [x] The human author has reviewed this PR in full and takes responsibility for its content.

comment.body:
@titaiwangms Addressed the eager replay storage in `1e72a57e3`: scatter mean now takes a replayable iterator factory, traversing updates once normally and again only for failed floating destinations. Tests check traversal counts and release of earlier ordinary updates. For a synthetic 100,000 float32 scalar updates to one destination, traced peak allocations dropped from 8,800,321 to 1,265 bytes (input arrays allocated before tracing). Overflow replay still stores contributions for failed destinations; this is not a bounded-memory guarantee.

The `k=0` wording clarifies the existing contract: v18 permits k up to rank(data), specifies trailing r-k slice dimensions, and its pseudocode indexes with `tuple(indices[idx])`, including the empty tuple. Added v18 whole-tensor regressions for all five existing reductions. The spec defines the mathematical mean and output conversion, not a particular floating summation algorithm; the reference's widened accumulation and finite-overflow fallback do not impose a new intermediate-precision mandate. The shared `_mean` fix intentionally also affects ReduceMean reference consumers, including expanded MVN; ordinary finite and nonfinite-input paths are unchanged.

For #8692, one temporary isolated combined native tree passed 361 tests (41 skipped), with regenerated docs and clean lint. Source tree `ea2f94c3ae961b8fb0436264e2fb17213b89fd87` combines this branch's `4da572fc7bf92c96236da2bbd9c3c5b290b4f849` (main `2ecdc8c6dcf3c8829b23df71f1383d230da700ed`) and #8692's `a425f56006aa8978e5ead058465d52f5e5d73be3`, plus its `15f04cd7481582ae6d6f8feae691db170c64ed5d` version-only doc additions and this commit's streaming delta. Checks covered exactly one v18 and one v29 schema, mean with int32/int64 indices and negative aliases/integer flooring, compatible reductions, and mean rejection before index access/Cast. Both branches' exporters were retained; reconciliation patches are saved as session artifacts, not published commits.

The proposed landing order remains #8692 first, then this PR syncing main and extending `ScatterNDSchema(bool allow_int32_indices, bool allow_mean=false)` for v29 only. Preserve the single v18 factory call and replace the ScatterND downgrade registration with one composed `NDIndices_29_28` adapter whose mean guard precedes widening; do not register a second adapter. The second PR to land must perform that reconciliation. The independent published branches do not yet compose, and this validation is not merge authorization or Operators SIG approval.

Fixed in f2d010f9d2d49093582165ea917d46bfa0e81e58. The 28→29 guard now includes decay input 4. A checker-valid gated_delta regression with unknown Q/K widths and decay `[1,1,0]` reproduced the missed rejection before the fix and now receives the explicit retain-opset-28 conversion error.

issue.body:
### Motivation and Context

Expert weights commonly use `[G, N, K]` storage: each output channel has a contiguous row of K input weights. In a quantized MoE model export, GGUF IQ2_XXS expert banks naturally decode to this layout because their quantization blocks run along K. GroupedMatMul currently requires `[G, K, N]`, so each expert projection needs an explicit `Transpose([0, 2, 1])` between dequantization and GroupedMatMul.

Add optional `transB` so GroupedMatMul can consume that natural weight orientation directly, following Gemm's convention. This removes the explicit layout adapter and simplifies dequantization-plus-grouped-matmul fusion. Repacking the quantized weights into the opposite orientation is not a simple byte transpose: it changes which values share quantization blocks and scales. A backend can already fuse the explicit transpose, so this is not a claim of guaranteed speedup; it makes the common layout directly expressible without requiring that extra fusion pattern.

The default `transB=0` preserves `[G, K, N]`; non-zero accepts `[G, N, K]` and logically transposes only the last two weight axes. Input `[M, K]`, output `[M, S, N]`, group indices, and optional bias `[G, N]` are unchanged.

Updates the current opset-29 proposal's schema, shape inference, context-dependent reference function, proposal documentation, generated documentation, and focused coverage. No new opset version, `transA`, or fused quantized operator is introduced.

issue.title: feat(defs): propose logcumsumexp for opset 29
issue.body:
### Motivation and Context

Propose `LogCumSumExp` for opset 29 to compute numerically stable cumulative log-sum-exp.

Relates to microsoft/onnxscript#3124: the current global-max-shift export turns `[-200, -100, 100]` into `[-inf, -inf, 100]` instead of approximately `[-200, -100, 100]`. The operation is available in [PyTorch](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.logcumsumexp.html) and [TensorFlow](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/math/cumulative_logsumexp), and used in [TorchSurv's Cox likelihood](https://github.com/Novartis/torchsurv/blob/bfbb64a75d6720ea8bc6b1cc990f53245a73d810/src/torchsurv/loss/cox.py#L27-L49) and the reported CTC decoding workload.

- `Y = LogCumSumExp(X, axis=0)`: inclusive forward prefixes, with an integer axis attribute and support for negative axes, dynamic shapes, and empty dimensions. Input rank is at least one; output shape and dtype match the input.
- Supports float16, bfloat16, float32, and float64 with promoted accumulation and defined NaN/infinity behavior.
- Includes a stable standard-op `Scan` fallback, Python reference implementation, shape inference, backend and converter coverage, and generated documentation.

The named operator lets runtimes select efficient CPU/GPU scan kernels directly. A global shift is unstable, while stable `Scan` or unrolled step-doubling exports incur loop overhead or graph growth; the function body provides a portable fallback.
